title: Sell Mineral Rights in Washington, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Washington, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights in or near Washington, PA, the county seat? We buy Marcellus interests directly and pay cash, no landman pressure.
heroLead: Washington, PA has been the county seat and the courthouse town for as long as anyone's grandparents can remember, and it's also sitting right in the middle of one of the busiest wet-gas plays in the country.
intro: Washington is both the county seat of Washington County and one of the most heavily developed parts of the Marcellus wet-gas core, home to Washington & Jefferson College and the courthouse where nearly every mineral transfer, lease, and probate matter tied to land across the county eventually gets recorded. That combination makes this a place where families can usually get real answers about their mineral interests faster than almost anywhere else in the play.

Development around the city has been dense and sustained since Range Resources first proved out the wet-gas window here in the mid-2000s, and units in and around Washington have often seen multiple rounds of drilling as operators returned to established pads for infill wells.

sections.heading: The Courthouse Advantage
paragraphs: Because the Washington County recorder of deeds and register of wills both sit in the city itself, confirming a chain of title or resolving an old probate matter tends to move faster here than for families whose land sits in outlying parts of the county. That's a genuine advantage when you're getting ready to sell.
It doesn't mean every deed is simple, though. Decades of pooling, unit re-drawing, and generational splits still show up on plenty of Washington-area tracts.

sections.heading: Reading a Statement From One of the Busiest Units in the State
paragraphs: If your tract sits inside an active Washington-area unit, your statement should separate gross value, deductions, and net payment clearly. Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act guarantees a one-eighth floor on gross value, but post-production deductions upheld under Kilmer v. Elexco can still shrink your net check substantially depending on your specific lease terms.

sections.heading: How We Approach an Offer Here
paragraphs: We pull your deed history, confirm your interest against current unit and permit filings, review any statements you have, and give you a straightforward cash offer grounded in real production data. There's no pressure to decide quickly.

faqs.question: Does being near the courthouse make selling easier?
faqs.answer: It often speeds up title confirmation since records are close at hand, though overall timing still depends on how complicated your specific ownership history is.

faqs.question: Why has this area seen so much repeat drilling?
faqs.answer: Strong early production results encouraged operators to return for infill wells on many established pads, which is common in the most productive parts of the wet-gas core.

faqs.question: My royalty check seems small compared to the reported gas price. Why?
faqs.answer: Post-production deductions for gathering, compression, and transportation are the most common reason. We review your specific lease language to explain exactly what's being deducted.

faqs.question: Can you help resolve an old probate issue tied to my mineral interest?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because the register of wills is also located in Washington, resolving outstanding probate matters here is often more straightforward than in other counties.
